summary: A1 ignores stereochemistry; A2 encodes it locally with rapid decay in atom embeddings; LogP probe metrics are pipeline artifacts.

claims.claim: GRASP-A1 vectors for enantiomers are bit-identical (distance = 0.0), confirming the model lacks stereochemical input or ignores chiral tags.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]([CH3])([Cl])[NH2]` (chiral center). Prediction: `||v_orig - v_enant|| < 1e-5`. If true, A1 is stereo-blind.
claims.prediction: Vector difference should be exactly zero for all molecules with chiral centers. Any non-zero value implies data leakage or embedding noise >0.

claims.claim: GRASP-A2 encodes stereochemistry in latent space (distance = 0.003) but maintains high similarity between enantiomers, consistent with achiral property symmetry.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]([CH3])([Cl])[NH2]`. Prediction: `||v_orig - v_enant|| > 1e-5` for A2, but < 0.01 relative norm.
claims.prediction: A2 vectors must differ (non-zero distance) to reflect R/S flip in embeddings, yet remain close (<0.01 rel dist) compared to random noise.

claims.claim: Stereochemical signal is highly localized at Layer 0 and attenuates rapidly through the graph layers.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]([CH3])([Cl])[NH2]`. Prediction: Atom embedding distance at stereocentre (Bin 0) > neighbors (Bins 1-4+) in early layers.
claims.prediction: Layer 0 Bin 0 should be ~5x higher than Layer 6 Bin 0. Signal spreads to Bins 1+ by L=2 but decays.

claims.claim: LogP probe deltas (d_enant = 2.26) are artifacts of data pipeline mismatch, not chemical property differences.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]([CH3])([Cl])[NH2]`. Prediction: `d_rand` must be ~0 for identical inputs.
claims.prediction: If vectors are truly identical (rand perm), d_enant/d_diast should match d_rand. Current values indicate index misalignment in probe evaluation.

claims.claim: A2 does not strongly separate diastereomers from enantiomers in CLS token space relative to A1's baseline.
claims.test: SMARTS: `[C@H]([CH3])([Cl])[NH2]`. Prediction: `dist(diast) / dist(enant)` should be > 1 for chemically distinct diastereomers.
claims.prediction: If A2 captures stereochemistry well, Diast distance >> Enant distance. Ratio ~1 suggests similar vector perturbation magnitude.

trivial_explanations: The LogP probe `d_rand` = 2.26 for identical inputs is a pipeline bug (Supervisor Hint), not model behavior.
`n_meso_skipped`=32 molecules were symmetric; their enantiomer distance would be zero by definition, excluded from stats.
